text:
Commander night at Alex's house on Moraga Way in Orinda, Friday 28 August. Three-player pod: me, Alex, Stuart. Game three of four on the night.

Good hand, dense interaction, and I countered at the right moments — the deck did the thing it is built to do and still lost.

The archetype's own problem showed up plainly: making everyone draw also hands everyone answers to my counters. I am symmetrically fuelling the table's ability to fight me.

I lost the game losing Heliod, in a stack war. I countered a spell, Alex countered my counter; I cast Swords to Plowshares, Alex redirected it onto Heliod. Engine offline from there. Psychosis Crawler was on the battlefield with the pieces to grow it and I never got there.

The read is that the deck has TOO MANY AXES and not enough of any one of them. There are sharp concepts in here and I still believe in the shell, but it is spread thin.

WHAT IT NEEDS IS PROTECTION. Losing the commander takes the whole engine down and there is currently no answer to a counter war plus redirected removal. That is the rebuild direction: protection first, before adding any more axes.
